prompt_text: What is the best Airbnb or short term rental to book in Nashville for a family of four?
answer_verbatim:
I can help pick the best short‑term rental for your family — but to give a specific listing I need a few details. Meanwhile here’s a practical guide and recommendations so you can find the ideal Airbnb for a family of four in Nashville.

Quick questions so I can narrow options:
- Dates (or month)?
- Budget per night or total?
- Kids’ ages?
- Will you have a car / need parking?
- Do you want to be near downtown attractions (Broadway), or prefer quieter neighborhoods / yards?
- Any must-have amenities (crib, fenced yard, washer/dryer, full kitchen)?

Best neighborhoods for families
- Germantown — historic, walkable, quiet streets, close to downtown and the riverfront. Good for short drives to major sites.
- 12South — very family friendly with parks, coffee shops, and boutiques; great for walking and photos.
- Hillsboro Village / West End — near Centennial Park (Parthenon), museums, and good restaurants; central and calm.
- East Nashville — more artsy, roomy rental houses, good for families who want a local vibe.
- Green Hills / Brentwood / Bellevue — suburban options with yards, more bedrooms, and quieter nights (better if you have a car).
- Donelson / Opryland — convenient to the airport and Opry, good if you plan to visit Opry/Midtown events.

What to filter for on Airbnb/VRBO
- Entire home or entire townhouse (no shared spaces)
- 2+ bedrooms or sleeps 4+ (confirm actual bed layouts)
- Superhost (Airbnb) or highly rated host
- Instant Book if you want quick confirmation
- Free parking or dedicated spot (if you’re driving)
- Washer/dryer, full kitchen
- Air conditioning (Nashville summers can be hot)
- Kid-friendly listing: crib/pack‑and‑play, high chair, fenced yard
- Recent reviews in the last 3–6 months (to check condition/changeover)
- Quiet/house rules and cancellation policy that work for you

Family-friendly features to prioritize
- Separate bedrooms with real beds (not one sofa pullout + one bed)
- Fenced yard or safe outdoor play area if kids are young
- Blackout curtains, soundproofing for early risers/nightlife nearby
- Easy access to grocery stores and family restaurants
- Ground-floor or elevator access if you have strollers or mobility concerns
- Fast Wi‑Fi and streaming TV for downtime

Booking tips
- Read several recent reviews for cleanliness and host responsiveness.
- Ask the host questions: exact sleeping arrangement, baby gear availability, parking details, noise in the evening.
- Check total price (cleaning fee, service fee, taxes) and cancellation terms.
- If you’re attending an event (Opry show, NFL game, festival), book early — Nashville fills fast.
- Consider a short-term rental with an easy self-check-in code if arrival times are late.

If you want, I can:
- Search and recommend 3–5 current listings (I’ll need dates and budget).
- Suggest exact addresses/areas based on attractions you’ll visit (zoo, Opry, downtown, etc.).

Tell me dates, budget, kids’ ages, and whether you want downtown walkability or a quieter neighborhood, and I’ll find tailored options.
